preconditions.description: The first line of stdin contains an integer t representing the number of test cases, where t is at least 1.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and 3 <= n <= 100 for n in test_case_ns)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the input contains an integer n where 3 <= n <= 100, representing the number of players to select from 2n total players.
The sum of squares of n over all test cases does not exceed 10,000.

preconditions.expression: all(outcome in ['>', '<'] for outcome in match_outcomes)
preconditions.description: For every match query '? i j', the response from stdin is either '>' (player i is stronger) or '<' (player j is stronger).

postconditions.expression: len([line for line in stdout_lines if line.startswith('?')]) <= 4 * n**2
postconditions.description: The number of match queries ('? i j') printed for a test case with parameter n does not exceed 4n^2.
The program outputs exactly one line starting with '!' to signal the end of the current test case.

postconditions.expression: len({p for p in range(1, 2*n + 1) if is_top_n(p, match_results)}) == n
postconditions.description: Based on the match results, there exists exactly one set of n players that must be the top n strongest players (i.e., every player in this set is stronger than every player not in this set).

There are at least two distinct valid orderings of the identified top n players consistent with the match results, meaning the relative strength of at least two players within the top n set is not determined.
